The behavior source is the `vendor/upstream/0.15.36/pstack/` snapshot at `c742dd61706fbacc1b95f1a20b7b988cf096ce6c`. Generated supported Skill/playbook entrypoints retain the upstream Markdown after this Pi prelude. The eleven core workflows have critical-rule mappings; preserving a source body does not prove that a model followed it. The full source inventory is pinned separately; maintainer semantic sign-off remains pending.

Apply user instructions and repository authority first. Read referenced source Markdown through `pstack_skill` with `upstream/skills/<skill>/...` resource IDs, consuming every page. Statechart's 0.15.36 TypeScript runtime and its test corpus are bundled under `skills/statechart/scripts`; the older 0.15.32 `.mjs` tools are retained for compatibility. Java/TLC and optional renderers are external dependencies. Other Cursor plugins, private APIs, drivers and cloud resources are not supplied.

This compiled copy is required in installed packages because Node does not strip TypeScript inside `node_modules`. The upstream source and test corpus remain unchanged.

## Platform substitutions

- Task workers use `pstack_agents` and `pstack_workflow` Pi AgentSessions. The parent owns the playbook. Parallel writers use Git worktrees; integrated delivery uses an explicit integrator and verification. These are local processes, not cloud VMs or OS sandboxes.
- `/setup-pstack` previews model roles and suggested panels using models visible in the current Pi session; edit only what needs changing. Existing choices are preserved. Panels with the same model in several seats do not provide model diversity. Model roles use `models.json`; pass the playbook and, for named roles such as Reflect's `tooling`, `judgment`, `divergent`, and `synthesizer`, `modelRole` when dispatching. Explicit node models take precedence.
- Pi `thinkingLevel` replaces Cursor's reasoning slug conventions. Optional same-family fallback chooses a registered model from the same provider and reports it; a supported lower reasoning level may be used and reported. Unknown families are not guessed, Cursor `-fast` aliases are not rewritten, and authentication/inference failures are not automatically retried.
- For an unconfigured panel, plans suggest available Pi models and disclose repeated seats. Unresolvable configured seats are dropped or replaced with an available survivor or the parent, with notes. A known-family parent gets a judge only from another recognized family; if none is available, the plan produces candidates only and the coordinator must inspect, choose, integrate and verify them. A failed or unaccepted candidate is excluded only after the other candidates settle; verified survivors remain eligible and the dropout is recorded.
- Arena's cross-judge uses confined `pstack_candidates` access to verified worktrees. The integrator independently reads and compares candidates before selecting and grafting. Architect's template includes a separate implementation phase after the selected sketch; the coordinator still owns upstream grounding (`how`/`why`) and optional checkpoints.
- Interrogate creates a worktree for each adversary, copies the reviewed staged, unstaged and untracked changes, and runs a separate repro-verifier on each worktree. No adversary changes are integrated. Both sessions must report command, observed and expected output; synthesis can only carry reproductions present in a verifier report. These sessions use Pi's ordinary writable-agent shell permissions; the verification-policy allowlist controls native gate commands, not their interactive shell. Model reports are not independently attested receipts: the coordinator must inspect actual command evidence and the effect of any repro edits before claiming a finding is verified.
- Swarm supports partition, best-of, first-pass and rank-all race templates. First-pass waits for a candidate's deterministic acceptance, requests cooperative cancellation of the remaining sessions, and waits for them to settle. Rank-all reports every rank without automatically integrating a winner. Mixed partition/race still needs an explicit DAG.
- Custom Mode maps to sticky `/poteto-mode`. `/loop` maps to `/pstack-loop`, which requires an active Pi host and cannot promise cloud-root scheduling or exact delivery across a crash.
- Use an available named CLI/UI driver for real-surface proof. Without one, return blocked or inconclusive with the exact reason; unit tests, fake providers and worker reports cannot replace a live lane.

## Explicit policy deviations

- Native exact-head/base ledgers invalidate verification when either changes, including patch-preserving restacks; upstream can reuse some patch-ID-stable verdicts.
- Read-only reviewer, scout and verifier sessions inspect confined source and evidence but cannot run shell commands or live MCP. Deterministic commands run in an authorized runner or writable lane. For external investigation, the parent supplies evidence snapshots and verifies decisive citations.
- Autopilot templates prepare local DAG artifacts. The coordinator remains responsible for the owner lifecycle, early PRs, periodic audit, rebase discipline, countersigns and stop propagation. A stack template alone does not deliver a remote PR stack. Babysit stops at merge-ready; shipping and remote writes require the actual applicable authorization.
- Opening a PR does not start a babysit. Finish the phase or stack before a requested babysit unless an explicitly assigned full-autonomy owner owns the loop and has reported code-ready. Babysit stops before merge; operator-reserved items never merge automatically.

## Unsupported operations

`Cursor-private-PR-provenance`, `Cursor-watch-READY`, `Cursor-cleanup-plugin` and `Bugbot-pass-dismissal` are unsupported. GitHub/Origin and native states are alternatives with their own evidence boundaries, not proof that a Cursor operation ran. `make-bot-ui` and the Cursor automation event pack require Cursor-specific surfaces. Report these limitations rather than marking unavailable operations complete.

## Evidence boundary

`SEMANTICS.json` records selected critical-rule mappings, exact source lines, deviations, bound tests and file fingerprints. Inventory counts, source hashes, deterministic checks, Pi SDK/fake-provider tests, real-model runs and maintainer semantic review are separate evidence levels. Advancing the source pin and passing CI do not establish complete Cursor/Pi equivalence or maintainer approval.


## Pi question interaction

Cursor `AskQuestion` is not a Pi tool supplied by this package. Ask in chat using clearly described options and let the user reply in their own words. For multiple selections, explicitly invite any combination; do not claim a multi-select UI was shown. Preserve the user’s answers before proceeding.

# Automate me

A guided flow for turning the user's working conventions into a skill agents will follow. The output is one `-mode` skill tailored to them (e.g. `jay-mode`, `priya-mode`).

This skill orchestrates three others: an inline mining pass (see step 1), Cursor's built-in `create-skill` (authoring), and the **unslop** skill (prose discipline). It sequences them. It doesn't replace them.

## Flow

### 0. Check for an existing skill

Look recursively for `.cursor/skills/**/*-mode/SKILL.md` and `~/.cursor/skills/*-mode/SKILL.md` matching the user's handle. Mode skills can live in a personal category directory (`.cursor/skills/<handle>/`), not only at the top level. If one exists, confirm intent with `AskQuestion` (unless they already said "update my skill" or similar):

- Update the existing skill (default for repeat runs)
- Start fresh (rare, ask why before doing it)

Update mode changes the rest of the flow:
- Step 1 mines only history since the skill was last edited (`git log -1 --format=%cI <path>`).
- Step 2 asks what's changed or missing, not what to capture from zero.
- Step 4 edits the existing file in place. Preserve sections the user hasn't contradicted. Revise ones with new evidence. Add new sections only for genuinely new rules.

### 1. Mine their history

Locate the active workspace's transcripts before fanning out. The system prompt names the workspace's `agent-transcripts/` directory. Use only that path. Don't glob across `~/.cursor/projects/*/`. That crosses workspace boundaries and reads private chats from unrelated projects.

Survey recent agent conversations within that scope for recurring patterns. Run multiple parallel subagents across slices of history (e.g. last 2-4 weeks, split into 3 slices so each has enough material). Pick each subagent's reasoning level and fast or standard speed for the job, per the Subagents section of the **poteto-mode** skill. Each slice mining subagent reads transcripts from the workspace-scoped path the parent provides, looks for the signals below, and returns a short structured list of patterns it saw with evidence pointers. Default signals worth hunting:

- Response preferences (length, tone, format, "dumb it down" corrections)
- Delegation habits (subagents, models, specialized workflows, parallelism)
- Verification posture (what "done" means, unit tests vs live repro, reviewers)
- Code and prose discipline (style, principles cited, lint/format tools)
- Process conventions (worktrees, commits, PRs, review/merge tooling)
- Meta preferences (fixing skills mid-task, proposing new ones)

Cross-check across slices before elevating a signal. Patterns seen in 2+ slices are high-confidence. Lone signals are weak and usually get dropped.

### 2. Ask the user directly

Mining misses intent that hasn't come up yet. Use the `AskQuestion` tool (structured multi-choice) rather than asking the user to type from scratch.

Shape: one or two questions with 4-6 options each, `allow_multiple: true` for category questions. Start broad ("Which areas matter most?"), then follow up on selected areas with specific options. After the structured rounds, one free-form chat question catches anything the options missed.

Don't dump 20 questions.

### 3. Cluster findings

Group the combined signals into sections. Common ones (use only what applies):

- **Response style**: length, tone, format.
- **Autonomy**: how much to do without asking, MCP tool use.
- **Understand first**: which skills to reach for when scoping or investigating a change.
- **Subagents**: default, parallelism, model-to-task, specialized workflows.
- **Prose / code discipline**: principles, lint tools, style guides.
- **Review and verify**: repro posture, verification skills, live-testing tools.
- **Process**: git worktrees, commits, PRs, review/merge tooling.
- **Skills**: skill-authoring habits, fix-the-skill-first, proposing new skills.

The **poteto-mode** skill shows the shape. Read it for granularity. Don't copy its content. The user's rules are not the same as poteto-mode's.

### 4. Draft the skill

Use Cursor's built-in `create-skill` skill to author the skill. Placement:

- Path: preserve an existing mode skill's category. For a new mode, use `.cursor/skills/<handle>/<handle>-mode/SKILL.md` when the repo has an established personal category for that handle. Otherwise default to `.cursor/skills/<handle>-mode/SKILL.md` in the project (or `~/.cursor/skills/<handle>-mode/` if the user prefers a personal skill).
- Handle: the user's first name or chosen identifier.
- Frontmatter `description`: trigger on their name + `/<handle>-mode` + "work in their style", not on generic keywords like "write code" or "review PR".
- Frontmatter formatting: follow `create-skill`'s YAML rules. Keep `description` as one YAML scalar. Quote it or use `description: >-` with indented continuation lines when punctuation or wrapping requires it.
- Frontmatter `disable-model-invocation: true` by default. Opt out only if the user explicitly wants their mode to apply on every turn.

### 5. Iterate on prose

Apply the **unslop** skill and `create-skill`'s writing guidelines to every line.

Show the draft to the user and take feedback. Expect multiple iterations. Cut ruthlessly. A mode skill is not a manual.

### 6. Land it

Work in a worktree off main. Commit and open a PR. Don't push to main directly.

## Guardrails

- **Don't overfit to one conversation.** A preference stated once and contradicted another time is noise. Require multiple instances before codifying it.
- **Don't be clever.** Restating other skills' contents, inventing metaphors, or writing "poetic" prose for an agent reader is cost without benefit. Keep it operational.
- **Reference, don't inline.** Other skills the user relies on should appear as path references, not pasted excerpts. Same for any principle docs they maintain elsewhere.
- **Keep sections minimal.** Only add a section if the user has a specific, non-default rule there. "Communicate clearly" is not a section. "Short paragraphs. Tables when comparing options. Bullets only when items are genuinely parallel." is.
- **Name conventions generic.** Use "the user" or "the human" in imperatives, not the author's first name.
- **Don't force symmetry.** If a user has no process rules worth writing down, skip the Process section entirely.

## Evaluation

A `-mode` skill is subjective output. A `create-skill`-style test/iterate benchmark loop isn't useful here. Vibe-check with the user: does it read like them? Did it miss anything? Then ship.

Run a description-optimization loop only if the skill's trigger accuracy turns out to be a problem in practice.

## When not to use

- User wants a task-specific skill (not working conventions): `create-skill` alone, no mining required.
- User wants to capture one narrow workflow (e.g. "how I write commit messages"). That's a regular skill, not a mode skill.



## Pi execution tools

Use `pstack_agents` for one child and `pstack_workflow` / `pstack_graph` for an explicit DAG. Roles are `architect`, `worker`, `reviewer`, `verifier`, `synthesizer` and `integrator`. Parallel writers use isolated worktrees, then an integrator. A verifier directly depends on the artifact owner. Inspect workflow status on recovery; completed nodes are not replayed. Check remote state before retrying external effects. `pstack_worktrees` cleans only owned clean worktrees.
